grandparents_cupboard.reason: Butter, eggs, honey, yoghurt, almonds, grapes and spices are all ordinary home staples with nothing factory-made.

supermarket.reason: Ground and flaked almonds, Greek yoghurt and red grapes are on every Tesco shelf; the almonds cost a little more but are not a specialist buy.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a loaf tin, bowl and whisk, and a one-bowl mix is well within a beginner's reach.

works.reason: The ratio of 250g ground almonds to 4 eggs and 150g yoghurt is sound for a moist gluten-free loaf, and 45 to 50 minutes at 180°C suits a 900g tin, giving plenty of slices for four.

honest_times.reason: Fifteen minutes covers melting butter, lining the tin, zesting and halving 300g grapes, and 55 minutes matches the bake plus a little margin.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed item, including lemon zest, cinnamon and salt, appears in the steps, and flaked almonds and red grapes are honest names for their ids.

seasonal_feel.reason: A warm baked loaf studded with 300g grapes suits late November, and the grapes are clearly the point of the dish.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are short, clear British English with no restaurant language or health preaching.

hearty_healthy.reason: Eggs, almonds, yoghurt and plenty of fruit with only 3 tbsp honey make a filling, low-sugar breakfast a family would happily repeat.
